title: Notification, Consent, and Data Inventory Semantics
authorityBoundary: This artefact defines app-surface data inventory, notification UI, consent receipt, audit event, and regional ads consent semantics. It does not create notification implementation, push provider integration, service worker implementation, ad SDK implementation, CMP implementation, legal conclusions, policy publication, provider configuration, store submission, ads compliance, privacy compliance, production readiness, live-provider readiness, product UI readiness, or human acceptance.

dataInventoryModel.rule: Every app-surface capability mapping must identify data inventory requirements for fields, commands, queries, events, telemetry, storage, notifications, ads, and store disclosures before implementation or disclosure claims.
mustReject: capability without data inventory mapping
field without privacy data category mapping
event without privacy data category mapping
notification without data inventory mapping
ads surface without consent and data inventory mapping
store disclosure impact without semantic backing

notificationInboxToastBannerModel.rule: Notification inbox, toast, and banner UI are transient or persistent projections of governed notification semantics and must map to capability, semantic event, consent, preference, permission, privacy, audit, i18n, accessibility, telemetry, and proof requirements.
mustReject: notification UI without capability mapping
notification UI without consent or preference mapping
notification UI without privacy mapping
notification UI without i18n or accessibility mapping
persistent inbox item without retention mapping

consentReceiptAndAuditEventModel.rule: Consent state must be tied to governed purposes, versions, withdrawals, receipts, audit events, actor, tenant boundary, and proof expectations.
mustReject: consent state without governed purpose
consent state without version
withdrawal without audit event
receipt without actor or tenant boundary
consent-dependent behaviour without proof

regionalAdsConsentModel.rule: Regional ads consent semantics must identify region, age or child-directed posture, personalised ads, non-personalised ads, consent purpose, audit event, privacy category, proof, dependencies, and non-claim boundaries before ad behaviour is accepted.
mustReject: ads behaviour without regional consent mapping
ads behaviour without age or child-directed posture
personalised ads without consent purpose mapping
ads event without privacy category mapping
ads claim without proof and non-claim boundary

validatorRequirements.description: Reject a capability, field, command, query, event, telemetry item, storage item, notification, ads surface, or store disclosure impact without data inventory and privacy data category mapping.
Reject notification inbox, toast, or banner UI without capability, consent or preference, permission, privacy, audit where required, i18n, accessibility, telemetry, and proof mappings.
Reject consent state, withdrawal, receipt, or consent-dependent behaviour without governed purpose, version, audit event, actor, tenant boundary, retention, and proof mappings.
Reject ads behaviour when consent, region, age or child-directed posture, personalised or non-personalised ads posture, privacy, audit, and proof mappings are missing.

proofRequirements.description: Future proof must demonstrate that data inventory, notification UI, consent receipt, audit event, and regional ads consent records are semantically mapped and fail closed when required mappings are absent.

implementationEvaluationRequirements: data inventory mappings exist for relevant capabilities and app surfaces
notification, consent, audit, and ads consent mappings exist where applicable
validator requirements are implemented and selftested
planted-defect fixtures exist for missing data inventory, notification, consent, and ads consent mappings
proof evidence exists for mapped and rejected cases
owner acceptance is recorded before any compliance, store, notification, ads, production, live-provider, product UI, or readiness claim
